context: git clean: -n previews, -d includes untracked directories, and -x also removes ignored files such as .env and local caches. Those are exactly the files with no copy in history, so -x deserves the preview most.
instruction: Preview deleting untracked files, directories, and ignored files.

context: ollama: list shows locally pulled models with their size and digest. ollama ps shows which are loaded into memory right now, which is the one that matters for VRAM pressure. ollama ships no man page.
instruction: List the models currently downloaded locally.

context: df: -i reports inode usage rather than bytes, which is the explanation when writes fail at apparently low utilization. -h formats the counts with unit suffixes.
instruction: Diagnose a disk-full error when there is clearly free space.

context: Zsh: zmv -n is a dry run that prints each intended rename without performing it. -i prompts per file and -f forces overwriting. Running -n first is the standard guard against a bad capture group.
instruction: Preview renaming every *.jpeg file to the same basename with .jpg.

context: pgrep: -f matches against the entire command line rather than just the process name, which is required for interpreted scripts. -a prints the matched command alongside the PID.
instruction: Find PID and command for processes matching python.*server.py.

context: ss -s prints totals per protocol and TCP state without listing individual sockets. A large TIME-WAIT count is normal; a growing CLOSE-WAIT count indicates an application not closing descriptors.
instruction: Get a summary count of sockets by state.

context: grep: -R follows all symbolic links during the walk; -r follows only links named on the command line. Both recurse, so the difference shows up when a subdirectory is a symlink. -n prefixes line numbers.
instruction: Search the whole src tree for TODO, following every symbolic link it encounters.

context: sort: -u drops duplicates as judged by the sort key, not the whole line, so -k2,2 makes uniqueness depend on column two alone. Writing -k2 without the end field extends the key to the end of the line.
instruction: Keep one line per user from accounts.tsv, comparing only the second column.

context: just --list prints every recipe with its doc comment, which is the fastest orientation in an unfamiliar repository. --show prints one recipe's body and --evaluate dumps variable values.
instruction: Discover what tasks a project defines.

context: ruff: format --check exits non-zero when a file would be reformatted and changes nothing on disk, which is the CI-safe mode. --diff additionally prints what would change.
instruction: Verify formatting in CI without rewriting any files.

context: perf top: -p targets an existing process, -e selects the cycles event, and -d sets the display refresh delay in seconds. Access can be restricted by perf_event_paranoid.
instruction: Watch cycle hotspots for process 4242, refreshing every two seconds.

context: Homebrew: uses lists formulae that depend on the named one, and --installed restricts that to what is actually present locally. Without --installed it searches the entire catalogue.
instruction: Find out which installed packages depend on openssl before removing it.

context: npm list: --depth=0 shows only top-level dependencies, where the default prints the entire tree. -g inspects globally installed packages instead of the project.
instruction: List directly installed packages without the whole dependency tree.

context: uv sync: --frozen installs from the lockfile and fails if it is out of date rather than silently updating it, which is what CI reproducibility requires. --no-dev omits development dependencies.
instruction: Install locked production dependencies in CI without re-resolving.

context: macOS: vm_stat reports Mach virtual memory counters in pages rather than bytes, so multiply by the page size it prints in the header. There is no free command in the base system.
instruction: Check memory pressure statistics on macOS.

context: BSD stat: -f supplies the format and %z is the byte size. GNU's -c %s means the same thing but neither spelling is accepted by the other implementation.
instruction: Print just the byte size of release.tar.gz on macOS.

context: awk: -F sets the input field separator, so -F: splits the colon-delimited passwd format. The !~ operator negates a regex match, and the $ anchors it to the end of the field.
instruction: List every user account that has a real login shell from /etc/passwd.

context: macOS base64: capital -D decodes and -i names the input file. GNU's lowercase -d is rejected. Scripts that must run on both platforms usually shell out to openssl base64 -d instead.
instruction: Decode a base64 payload stored in token.b64 on macOS.

context: journalctl: -b restricts the query to the current boot. A single -p priority includes that level and every more severe level, while --no-pager makes the output suitable for capture or piping.
instruction: Show warnings and more severe journal entries from the current boot without opening a pager.

context: jq: -r emits strings without surrounding quotes. select keeps only values matching the predicate, and \(...) interpolates expressions inside a string literal.
instruction: From an array of records in data.json, print the id and name of each entry whose status is active, as raw text.
